entries.speaker: gary-numan
entries.heard: and my wife got me this album for the first time and it changed everything for me, it's a fantastic album It made me love music again I didn't realize I'd sort of fallen out of love with it
entries.quote: My wife got me this album for the first time and it changed everything for me. It's a fantastic album. It made me love music again.
entries.citation: Gary Numan says on Amoeba Music's What's In My Bag? that Depeche Mode's Songs of Faith and Devotion "changed everything for me" and "made me love music again" when his career was in a bad place, and that his music has been heavier and darker since.
entries.note: Also at 3:08: 'Ever since I listened to this album, my music has been much heavier, much darker and more inventive.'

entries.speaker: gary-numan
entries.heard: A lot of people think I was influenced by Kraftwerk. I wasn't, actually other than it was electronic I think what they did was brilliant
entries.quote: A lot of people think I was influenced by Kraftwerk. I wasn't, actually, other than it was electronic. I think what they did was brilliant.
entries.citation: Gary Numan says on Amoeba Music's What's In My Bag? that "A lot of people think I was influenced by Kraftwerk. I wasn't, actually," and later that it "was no influence at all, just wasn't what I wanted to do."
entries.note: Directly contradicts the existing gary-numan -> kraftwerk edge. Second line at 4:12: 'but it was no influence at all, just wasn't what I wanted to do'.

entries.speaker: vampire-weekend
entries.heard: >> I have a memory of going to Paris with my dad on a on a business trip and I remember going to the Virgin Megastore and buying both of these albums at the
entries.quote: I have a memory of going to Paris with my dad on a business trip, and I remember going to the Virgin Megastore and buying both of these albums at the same time.
entries.note: He was 14 in 1997 and says the music you like from 13 to 24 stays with you, but says it generally, not that OK Computer shaped his music. Record named only as "this" (OK Computer, paired with Daft Punk Homework).
